subject: Post-demo: throughput targets & reserve path
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Todd Meyers <todd.meyers@stratasecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-19T14:03:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: throughput targets & reserve path

Todd,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — good conversation. This thread is a short recap + a couple of concrete asks so we can size an initial dedicated reservation that lines up with your procurement window.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: real-time chat assistant (low-latency): typical response ~450 tokens; current sustained ~80 reqs/sec; peak ~200 reqs/sec during batch windows.
- Secondary workload: async batch embedding/semantic search refresh (larger batches, higher token bursts but lower p95 latency tolerance).
- Target commercial: looking for a committed path that gets unit cost in the neighborhood of $18–$25 per 1M tokens, with an option to scale down/up. Procurement ideally this quarter.

Asks we need from you to finalize a concrete proposal
1) Confirm average tokens per response and typical peak concurrency (if the 200 reqs/sec peak is correct).
2) Confirm required p95 latency for the chat path (is 200–250ms acceptable? do you need sub-150ms?).
3) Confirm budget range and commitment term you prefer (12 vs 24 months).

What we propose next (high level)
- We'll sketch 3 reserved configurations (A100-optimized, H100-optimized, mixed) with expected throughput and a modeled $/1M tokens (proforma attached).
- Recommend a short tech deep-dive to validate exact request size distribution and KV-cache opportunities (30–45m).
- If you like the numbers, we can issue a HubSpot proposal and a DocuSign for a 12-month reservation to start.

I've attached a lightweight workbook with the token-econ model and a one-page proforma. If you can reply with the three items above, we'll produce a firm reserved SKU proposal by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: proforma_dedicated_sketch.pdf (1 page), token-econ-workbook.xlsx (xlsx)

Date: 2027-06-19T17:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput targets & reserve path

Sean — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications so the numbers you send map to how we run things: 

- Tokens & concurrency: 450 tokens average per assistant response is correct for the majority path. We see ~80 reqs/sec sustained and true peaks of ~180–200 reqs/sec for 3–5 minute bursts (daily). For stress tests we hit ~260 reqs/sec but that is a rare spike.
- Latency tolerance: our product SLAs are customer-facing. For the chat path we need p95 latency <= 250ms end-to-end; internal target is 200ms but we can accept up to 250ms if it helps economics.
- Budget & term: looking for a 12-month commitment to start. Budget target for committed unit economics is $18–$22 per 1M tokens for the committed baseline. If we can get lower at higher commit that's attractive.
- Procurement timeline: we start budget approvals next week; goal is to have a signed commitment within 3–4 weeks if all checks out.

One more ask: can you include expected fallback/overflow behavior in case reserved lanes are saturated? We want to understand how Redwood will maintain availability during those short daily bursts.

—Todd

Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput targets & reserve path

Todd — great, thanks for the specifics. Quick sketch below (numbers rounded) — I'll produce the full matrix and math in the attached CSV and the workbook.

Assumptions used
- Avg tokens per response: 450
- Sustained requests/sec: 80 (workload A)
- Peak bursts: 200 reqs/sec for ~5 minutes daily
- Token conversion: sustained tokens/sec = 80 * 450 = 36k tokens/sec; peak tokens/sec = 200 * 450 = 90k tokens/sec during burst

Throughput & GPU sizing (rough)
- 4 x H100 (reserved): handles ~40k sustained tokens/sec with comfortable p95 headroom for chat; expected p95 ~160–220ms depending on model/context length. Modeled unit cost ~ $28 / 1M tokens (baseline).
- 8 x H100 (reserved): handles ~85–95k tokens/sec sustained (covers your daily peaks); expected p95 ~140–200ms. Modeled unit cost ~ $16 / 1M tokens (12-mo commit).
- 12 x H100 (reserved): comfortable headroom for extra growth and redundancy; modeled unit cost ~ $12 / 1M tokens (12-mo commit + volume discount).

Fallback/overflow behavior
- Short bursts beyond reserved capacity will automatically route to a shared burst pool (elastic capacity) with a higher per-token price; we can cap burst spend by policy.
- We also support a degraded-mode rollout where requests are served by a smaller, quantized model variant for non-critical traffic to preserve latency/SLA for high-priority requests.

Tradeoffs and alternatives
- A100 80GB alternative: ~8% lower $/token on price but p95 increases ~40–60ms in our tests for this workload; that matters if you target sub-150ms.
- Mixed configuration (e.g., 6x H100 + 4x A100) can reduce cost while keeping tail latency for high-priority traffic on H100s.

Next steps I propose
1) We finalize the 3-option pricing matrix (attached reserved-pricing-matrix.csv).
2) Schedule a 30–45m tech deep-dive next week for your infra and SRE (we'll bring a perf engineer and an infra product manager).
3) I'll add a brief policy stub in the proposal that caps burst spend and defines fallback quantized model behavior.

Attachments: reserved-pricing-matrix.csv (CSV)

If 8 x H100 at ~$16/1M (12mo) looks reasonable I can push a HubSpot quote and get DocuSign ready for signature.

Thanks,
Sean
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Todd / Sean — quick internal note (replying all so Stratasecure sees the ask and our recommended path):

- Recommendation: start with the 8 x H100 reserved lane on a 12-month commitment. Rationale: covers your daily peaks (~200 reqs/sec -> ~90k tokens/sec) with p95 comfortably within your 200–250ms window for the chat path and gives room for KV-cache benefits.
- Operational guardrails: include a hard burst-spend cap (we typically propose $X/month based on your peak windows) and an automatic 30-day usage review with a one-time option to add +4 GPUs at the same rate.
- Rollout plan: 1) sign and provision 2) 2-week pilot/canary (10–20% traffic) with a target SLA check 3) full cutover and a 90-day performance & econ review.

If Stratasecure agrees, we should lock the HubSpot draft and can issue a DocuSign contract (I can own the procurement coordination).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks — this all looks sensible and aligns with our internal direction. Confirming:

- We can commit to an initial 8 x H100 reservation for 12 months contingent on the following:
  * p95 latency for chat path at or below 250ms in production after the pilot (we accept up to 250ms).
  * SOC 2 Type II evidence and basic audit logs for request tracing (we'll share our security questionnaire separately).
  * Burst spend cap set (please propose a concrete dollar cap in the HubSpot quote).

- Procurement: we'll aim to sign within 3 weeks. Please create the HubSpot deal (STRAT-4721) and send a DocuSign when ready. We prefer the canary pilot before full cutover.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the pricing matrix and the pilot plan.

Todd
